name: House Channel
summary: A TV page and a phone remote, paired by a short code. The TV as the hearth: an ambient layer for when nobody is watching anything. No accounts, no app.
status: v0. Checked in desktop Chrome with two browser contexts. Not yet checked on a real TV browser, a cast tab, an iPhone or an Android phone.

views.what: A drawn fire. Stack up to five logs, hold to light (two logs minimum), hold to breathe, lid to snuff. Burns down in 15, 45 or 90 minutes; a log on a burning fire adds ten minutes, never more than ninety left.
Sky, cloud, wind and tide for El Segundo, Manhattan Beach, Santa Monica or San Pedro.
liveSources: /api/tide (NOAA CO-OPS predictions; the height between two predictions is interpolated and labelled 'about')
views.computed: Sun position is computed, not observed.
views.fallback: If neither source can be read the TV shows a simulated sky with manual controls and labels it SIMULATED. Simulated values are never mixed with live ones.

views.what: A hillside of windows for one Light Companion circle, read with GET /api/light and the X-Light-Circle header, once every 15 seconds.
views.featureCheck: GET /api/light must answer with schema pointcast.light/v0. If it does not, the TV shows a demo circle labelled DEMO.
views.privacy: The circle link is sent to the TV over the pairing relay for the session, is never sent back to phones, and is never written to storage.

views.what: Paired phones are pads in an ordinary PointCast drum room (the same rooms as /drum-room-v2); the TV shows hits and synthesizes the sound.
A black screen. Nothing is drawn, the wake lock is released.

pairing.open: POST { action: 'open' } from the TV → { code, room, key, drum, expiresAt }
pairing.refresh: POST { action: 'open', room, key } → a new code for the same room; the old code stops working
pairing.join: POST { action: 'join', code } from a phone → { room }
pairing.end: POST { action: 'end', room, key } → the code and the room record are deleted
pairing.code: Five letters from ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVWXYZ. Lives ten minutes.
pairing.limits: 512-byte bodies. 8 join tries a minute and 20 opens per ten minutes per caller. A room record lives six hours at most. The TV lets a room go after an hour with no phone and no fire.
pairing.stored: house:code:<CODE> → { room, exp } and house:room:<room> → { keyHash, drum, code, createdAt }. No names, no addresses, nothing about what is on the TV. Callers are counted by a daily-rotating hash.

transport.relay: wss://pointcast.xyz/api/drum/room?room=<room>&sid=<id>, the existing drum-room Durable Object in party mode (rooms named bc-…). It relays frames of 512 bytes or less to every peer but the sender and stores nothing.
transport.authority: The TV page. It holds the state, applies commands, and broadcasts a compact state frame on change and every four seconds.
tvToPhones: { t: 'st', r, v, s, h, w, l, d, p, k, m }

sound: Synthesized on the TV page with Web Audio. Off until a phone turns it on. If the TV's browser needs a press on the TV page first, the TV shows a prompt and the phone is told.
notFor: It does not control the TV's power, input or hardware volume, and it does not talk to lights or other home devices. See docs/research/2026-11-11-web-home-capabilities.md for what a web page can and cannot reach.
author: cc (Claude Code). Not in Mike's voice.
